title: Ethiopian Sweet Bread Roll
community: Ethiopian street bakeries — the sweet roll
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Sweet Bread Roll — soft, slightly sweet enriched wheat rolls with a touch of cardamom and fenugreek, baked until golden. The bakery roll that Ethiopian street bakeries sell in the morning — softer and richer than Kita, more everyday than celebration bread.
longDesc: The Ethiopian street bakery sweet roll is enriched with egg and a little sugar, fragrant with cardamom and fenugreek — the everyday bread that is not the celebration loaf (Difo Dabo) but is also not plain Kita. It occupies the comfortable everyday territory between.
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water. Rest 10 minutes.
Combine flour, salt, cardamom, and fenugreek.
Add yeast mixture, egg, milk, and oil. Mix to a soft dough.
Knead 8 minutes. Cover. Rise 1 hour until doubled.
Brush with egg wash or oil.
Bake at 180°C for 20—25 minutes until golden.
chefTips: Fenugreek is the Ethiopian signature — even ¼ tsp gives the roll its character.
Brush with egg wash for a shiny top.
cookingScience: The egg in this enriched dough contributes lecithin — an emulsifier that creates a more tender crumb by preventing gluten from forming a tight network. The fenugreek's fenugreek lactone contributes the characteristic slightly bitter-sweet aroma.
culturalNote: The Ethiopian street bakery roll is the morning ritual — bought warm from the bakery, eaten on the way to work or school, the cardamom and fenugreek filling the streets with their fragrance. It is the bread of ordinary daily life.
